answer: Each agent stakes a cryptographic token in a shared vault that timestamps every transaction; the ledger records a unique ripple of payment intervals that only a genuine voyage of activity can reproduce. When a new identity appears, the network checks its timing pattern against existing harbors of linked agents; a match merges it into the established kin‑link, otherwise it is rejected. An attacker must acquire enough tokens to mimic the exact interval ripple for every linked identity, making the cost scale linearly with the size of the targeted cluster.
